generated_from: 336 of 336 catalog problems, triaged by gpt-5.6-sol at high reasoning effort

queue.title: Shared Gamma conflates within- and between-study modification
queue.design_sketch: Vary the fraction of studies with IPD, the correlation between study-level covariate distributions and unmeasured study characteristics, and the difference between true within- and between-study interactions. Compare shared-Gamma and separated Gamma_W/Gamma_B models on bias and coverage of causal interaction and target-population treatment effects.
queue.priority_note: This deserves an early run because it tests a specific causal contamination mechanism using a standard within-between decomposition.

queue.title: Aggregate-data-only interactions may be prior-driven
queue.design_sketch: Generate component networks in which interactions have strong IPD information, aggregate curvature information only, weak information, or no likelihood information, and vary prior scale. Evaluate prior-to-posterior contraction and effective likelihood rank by their discrimination of these states and by coverage of downstream target contrasts.
queue.priority_note: This highly rated item is also a clean early experiment because diagnostic discrimination can be measured against known likelihood information.

queue.title: Priors, not data, can drive posteriors in weakly identified models
queue.design_sketch: Estimate a population-specific treatment contrast while varying overlap, network connectivity, interaction information and prior scale. Measure whether power-scaling, prior-to-posterior contraction and prior-only contrast comparisons detect likelihood weakness, using sensitivity to prior perturbation and contrast coverage as deciding measures.
queue.priority_note: This deserves an early run because it is focused, uses existing tools and directly distinguishes evidence-driven precision from prior-driven precision.

queue.title: Reported target moments are treated as known constants
queue.design_sketch: Estimate a target-population marginal treatment effect while varying target-summary sample size, source-target overlap, covariate correlation, and effect-modification strength; compare fixed-moment, target-summary variance, and perturbation intervals on bias, standard-error calibration, and 95% coverage.
queue.priority_note: This should run early because it is a clean, feasible evaluation of an identifiable omission with existing theory and implementable corrections.

queue.title: Nothing propagates sampling error in reported target moments
queue.design_sketch: Estimate a target-superpopulation marginal log odds ratio while varying the target aggregate sample size, covariance among reported moments, overlap, and effect-modification strength. Compare intervals that fix target moments with intervals using joint target-moment resampling or stacked estimating equations on bias, standard-error calibration, and 95% coverage.
queue.priority_note: This is a lower-complexity, decisive experiment with a clear estimand and should run early, especially before broader uncertainty-propagation projects.

queue.title: PAIC diagnostics are not evaluated as classifiers of realized error
queue.design_sketch: Prespecify a material-error threshold for the target marginal treatment effect, vary overlap, modifier misspecification and sample size, and evaluate each routinely reported diagnostic using area under the ROC curve, calibration and decision-curve performance.
queue.priority_note: This is one of the best early studies: the estimand, truth, predictor diagnostics and deciding performance measures can all be prespecified.

queue.title: The shared effect modifier check has low and uncalibrated power
queue.design_sketch: Estimate treatment-by-covariate interactions and target-population treatment effects while varying interaction drift, trials per treatment, IPD availability, covariate overlap and common versus exchangeable interaction priors. Measure the split-interaction check's type I error, power and calibration, plus the probability that undetected drift changes the treatment decision.
queue.priority_note: This is one of the strongest early studies because the diagnostic already exists, the truth is simulable and the result would directly determine when its apparent reassurance is meaningful.

queue.title: ML-NMR interactions can rest solely on aggregate-data variation
queue.design_sketch: Estimate within-person effect modification separately from between-study ecological association while varying the number and placement of IPD trials, disagreement between the two coefficients, covariate overlap and prior strength. Compare conventional, within-study-centered and hierarchically treatment-specific ML-NMR models on interaction bias, target-effect coverage and the sensitivity and specificity of identification flags.
queue.priority_note: This deserves an early run because it addresses a concrete ML-NMR failure mode with known truth and can produce practical minimum-IPD guidance.

queue.title: Non-proportional hazards and the transported hazard ratio
queue.design_sketch: Estimate target RMST differences, milestone survival differences, and time-varying marginal hazard ratios while varying baseline family, degree and timing of non-proportionality, effect-modifier overlap, and differential censoring. Compare proportional-hazards MAIC and STC with flexible survival ML-NMR on bias, interval coverage, survival-curve calibration, and instability of the reported constant hazard ratio.
queue.priority_note: This should run early because it is a decisive benchmark of existing estimators against a common but poorly aligned reporting practice.

queue.title: Failure signatures across PAIC estimator families are uncharacterized
queue.design_sketch: Vary effect-modifier overlap from near-complete to near-disjoint and cross it with interaction strength and outcome-model misspecification, comparing weighting and outcome-model estimators on bias, coverage, variance inflation and whether standard diagnostics signal failure before material error occurs.
queue.priority_note: This is a clean and consequential experiment, but the comparator set should be limited initially because adding doubly robust and flexible learners makes a one-week study unrealistic.

queue.title: Convenience functional forms and untested flexible alternatives
queue.design_sketch: Estimate a target-population marginal treatment effect while varying overlap, sample size, event rate, and adversarial response surfaces containing thresholds, splines, nonlinear treatment interactions, and covariate interactions. Compare parametric STC, spline-based STC, BART, and a doubly robust learner on bias, RMSE, interval coverage, and failure under extrapolation.
queue.priority_note: This is a strong and genuinely open benchmark, but its very high catalog rating does not make it a good first one-week project because valid inference across several flexible learners substantially enlarges the workload.

queue.title: Poisson aggregate likelihood needs zero exposure-rate covariance
queue.design_sketch: Vary the within-arm correlation between exposure time and rate-relevant covariates, follow-up dispersion, and effect-modification strength while holding total exposure fixed. Compare unweighted and exposure-weighted integration on bias and 95 percent coverage of target marginal rate ratios, and estimate the covariance threshold at which conclusions change.
queue.priority_note: Run very early despite its lower rating because it is a precise assumption with a fast, decisive simulation and directly actionable reporting implications.

queue.title: Design-dependent roles of prognostic covariates
queue.design_sketch: Estimate a target-population marginal risk difference, odds ratio, or hazard ratio under anchored and unanchored designs while varying prognostic strength, cross-study imbalance, and overlap. Compare adjustment through MAIC balancing versus outcome-model standardization on bias, interval coverage, precision, and effective sample size.
queue.priority_note: Run moderately early, but focus on non-collapsible marginal effects because the collapsible-scale result is already established and would make a repetitive study.

queue.title: No aggregate integration method for median-based covariate summaries
queue.design_sketch: Simulate skewed aggregate-study covariates, vary interaction strength, skewness, sample size, and whether summaries are median-range or median-IQR, then compare reconstruction methods and marginal families on bias and interval coverage of the target-standardized treatment effect.
queue.priority_note: Run very early because this is a clean, feasible experiment with a known truth and an immediate consequence for routine ML-NMR analyses.

queue.title: Per-comparator adjustment sets yield non-comparable PAIC contrasts
queue.design_sketch: Simulate one IPD trial and four aggregate-data comparators, varying effect-modifier strength, population overlap, and comparator-specific covariate reporting. Compare maximal per-comparator and common-intersection adjustment sets on bias, interval coverage, and the probability of producing an incorrect treatment ranking.
queue.priority_note: Run early: this is a clean, consequential PAIC experiment with directly actionable reporting and analysis implications.

queue.title: No criterion chooses pooled or arm-separate matching in anchored MAIC
queue.design_sketch: Vary aggregate-trial arm imbalance, prognostic strength of unmatched covariates, effect modification, and effective sample size; compare pooled and arm-separate MAIC on bias and coverage of the target marginal treatment effect and on post-weighting imbalance in unmatched covariates.
queue.priority_note: This is among the best early studies because the alternatives are explicit, the failure mechanisms are simulable, and bias and coverage give a decisive answer.

queue.title: Rare events, separation, and zero-event studies in weighted synthesis
queue.design_sketch: Vary event risk, treatment effect, covariate dimension and source-target overlap so that weight concentration and event counts change independently, then compare ordinary, penalized and Bayesian weighted binary models on bias, coverage and separation. Evaluate candidate effective-event-sample-size diagnostics by their ability to predict large error or failed coverage.
queue.priority_note: This is a strong early study because it is focused, readily simulated and can deliver both an estimator comparison and a directly testable diagnostic.

queue.title: No two-stage adjusted estimator carries multi-arm covariance
queue.design_sketch: Simulate three- and four-arm IPD trials while varying shared-arm size, covariate overlap, and effect modification, then compare independent contrast adjustment with a joint bootstrap or stacked estimating equations. Empirical within-study covariance, standard-error calibration, and 95 percent coverage of network contrasts decide whether the estimator works.
queue.priority_note: Run early despite the lower rating because it is a bounded estimator problem with a decisive coverage experiment and an immediately useful result.

queue.title: No inference is reported for an estimated optimal-treatment boundary
queue.design_sketch: Simulate ML-NMR data with one or two continuous effect modifiers, varying interaction strength, overlap, treatment separation, and proximity to the optimal-treatment boundary. From posterior draws, estimate profile-specific optimal-treatment probabilities and boundary bands, then assess coverage, boundary-location error, and treatment-assignment regret.
queue.priority_note: Run early: it is a focused PAIC problem with a clear estimand, observable performance criteria, and an implementable posterior-draw solution.

queue.title: ML-NMR runtime can constrain repeated sensitivity analyses at scale
queue.design_sketch: Estimate wall-clock cost and effective posterior draws per minute for ML-NMR while varying total integration rows, study count, covariate dimension, outcome model and random-effects structure. Fit a runtime prediction model and identify configurations that fail prespecified elapsed-time, convergence or Monte Carlo error thresholds.
queue.priority_note: This lower-complexity study should run early because it yields an immediately useful scaling map and can bound the feasibility of later ML-NMR simulations.

queue.title: Measurement error and component misclassification are ignored
queue.design_sketch: Estimate a target-population component-regimen contrast while varying effect-modifier measurement error, component misclassification probability, whether miscoding changes cross-subnetwork connectivity, and covariate overlap. Compare deterministic and probabilistic coding or calibration models on bias, coverage, topology-selection error, and the probability that the target contrast remains estimable.
queue.priority_note: This deserves an early run after narrowing to either covariate error or component miscoding; the latter offers an especially clear and consequential experiment.

queue.title: Bayesian component ML-NMR and bridge models lack SBC validation
queue.design_sketch: Draw parameters from the fitted hierarchical prior, simulate complete IPD, aggregate-arm and target structures, and refit the identical model. Assess calibration using rank statistics for decision contrasts plus data-dependent quantities such as the joint log-likelihood, while varying integration accuracy and identification strength.
queue.priority_note: Run after a reduced model and compute budget are fixed; it is decisive for implementation correctness but must not be presented as validation of scientific assumptions.

queue.title: No simulation crosses target choice with second-stage transport error
queue.design_sketch: Use a fractional-factorial simulation to vary index, comparator, pooled, registry, and overlap targets; correct versus misspecified second-stage transport; target-moment sample size; overlap; and shared versus treatment-specific effect modification, scoring bias and coverage against externally generated target-marginal truth.
queue.priority_note: This is a legitimate and decisive simulation increment, but it should follow smaller studies because the design and interpretation are too large for a credible one-week execution.

queue.title: Edge influence is approximate for multi-arm and random effects
queue.design_sketch: Estimate target-specific edge influence while varying multi-arm correlation, heterogeneity and network topology, then compare the current diagonal approximation with leave-one-edge-out refitting that re-estimates heterogeneity. Decide accuracy using influence-value error, rank correlation and identification of the truly most influential edge.
queue.priority_note: This is a clean and decisive diagnostic study that should run early because the approximation can be tested against an operational reference calculation.

queue.title: Conventional STC reports a conditional effect at target means
queue.answerable_part: The conditional-versus-marginal mismatch is already settled, but a simulation can quantify the residual bias and undercoverage caused by reconstructing an unknown target joint covariate distribution from published marginals.
queue.design_sketch: Target the marginal log odds ratio in the aggregate-study population while varying covariate correlation, copula family, overlap, and nonlinear effect modification under identical published means and standard deviations. Compare conventional mean-profile STC, g-computation using the true target law, and g-computation using independence, copula, or maximum-entropy reconstructions on bias and coverage.
queue.priority_note: The original very-high-priority claim would make a weak new study because it is solved, but the target-joint-law residual is a clean and highly feasible early simulation.

queue.title: Weak overlap leaves target regions the source data cannot support
queue.answerable_part: A simulation can compare diagnostics and abstention rules for detecting practically consequential lack of overlap, but no scalar diagnostic can certify support for every unreported or misspecified effect-modifying direction.
queue.design_sketch: Estimate a target marginal treatment effect while varying source-target overlap from strong to absent, the alignment of unsupported directions with true effect modification, covariate dimension, and outcome model misspecification. Compare Kish ESS, local ESS, density-ratio diagnostics, leverage, influence measures, and extrapolation scores on bias, coverage, diagnostic discrimination, and false-abstention rates across MAIC, STC, ML-NMR, ML-UMR, and NMI.
queue.priority_note: This deserves to run first because it is central to every population-adjustment method, supports a clean simulation, and can directly replace misleading reliance on a single global ESS.

queue.title: Two-stage component PAIC adjusts only the IPD edges
queue.answerable_part: A simulation can quantify the bias caused by mixing population referents and test a one-stage alternative, but it cannot establish how often the required aggregate covariate distributions are recoverable in practice.
queue.design_sketch: Simulate component networks while varying the proportion of IPD edges, population separation, effect-modification strength, and accuracy of reconstructed aggregate covariate distributions. Compare two-stage component MAIC or STC with one-stage component ML-NMR on bias and interval coverage for a target-population marginal treatment contrast.
queue.priority_note: This is a strong early simulation because the competing architectures make distinct, testable predictions under controlled population shifts.

queue.title: Deciding which covariates are true effect modifiers
queue.answerable_part: A simulation can compare prespecified modifier-selection strategies within a defined class of causal structures, but no study can identify a universally correct modifier set independent of contrast, scale, estimand and clinical knowledge.
queue.design_sketch: Estimate a target-population marginal treatment contrast while varying interaction sparsity, modifier strength, source-target imbalance, overlap and sample size. Compare expert-oracle sets, all-covariate adjustment, significance screening, penalized interactions and stability selection on bias, coverage, effective sample size and selection stability.
queue.priority_note: This is highly important but too broad as stated; run early only after narrowing it to a few defensible selection strategies and a declared estimand.

queue.title: Intervals omit selection, reconstruction and target-summary error
queue.answerable_part: One study can determine the coverage loss from a specified omitted uncertainty source, especially target-summary uncertainty, but jointly resolving selection, reconstruction, structural and prior uncertainty is too broad.
queue.design_sketch: For a marginal target-population treatment effect, vary target-summary sample size, covariance availability and source-target overlap, then compare conditional intervals with bootstrap or joint-model intervals on bias, interval coverage and width.
queue.priority_note: Narrow to target-summary uncertainty and run early; attempting every uncertainty source at once would turn a strong question into an uninterpretable factorial.

queue.title: PAIC simulations generate only shared, linear effect modification
queue.answerable_part: A focused simulation can settle robustness to treatment-specific or nonlinear effect modification, but the full list of support, measurement, target-definition, ecological and participation mechanisms cannot be resolved in one study.
queue.design_sketch: For a marginal target-population treatment effect, vary shared linear, treatment-specific and threshold effect modification while holding reported covariate moments fixed, then compare PAIC methods on bias, coverage and decision error.
queue.priority_note: This lower-complexity slice deserves an early run because it directly tests assumptions that existing simulations often build in and can produce a decisive robustness result.

queue.title: Narrow outcome families and hazard-ratio-only survival scoring
queue.answerable_part: A focused study can determine whether hazard-ratio scoring conceals clinically important survival-curve and RMST error under nonproportional hazards; it cannot cover every listed outcome family defensibly in one study.
queue.design_sketch: Vary effect-modifier overlap and the degree of delayed, waning, or crossing treatment effects, then compare MAIC, STC, and ML-NMR on bias and coverage for target-population survival probabilities and RMST, alongside log hazard-ratio bias. The decisive result is whether methods with acceptable hazard-ratio error still have large integrated survival-curve or RMST error.
queue.priority_note: Run the nonproportional-survival slice early because it is clinically important and yields a clean, decisive comparison, while postponing the much broader outcome-family catalog.

queue.title: QBA is judged on oracle recovery, not honest classification
queue.answerable_part: A study can measure robustness-classification performance conditional on explicit models for elicitation error and sensitivity-set construction; it cannot establish unconditional honesty without evidence about how analysts or experts actually elicit those inputs.
queue.design_sketch: Simulate an unanchored target-population treatment effect and sensitivity sets with varying width, dependence, centering error, and probability of excluding the truth, then classify each result as robust or fragile under a fixed decision threshold. Score false reassurance, false fragility, truth inclusion, tipping-point error, probabilistic interval coverage, decision reversal, and expected regret.
queue.priority_note: Run this early as a focused experiment because false reassurance is the central QBA failure and the classification estimand is much cleaner than a broad multi-bias factorial.

queue.title: The MAIC paradox: swapping the IPD trial can reverse the comparison
queue.answerable_part: The study can identify configurations that cause sign reversal and demonstrate the consequence in an appraisal, but it cannot estimate its frequency across sponsor submissions or settle the procedural rule committees should adopt.
queue.design_sketch: Hold the covariate set fixed, swap which trial supplies IPD, and vary target-mean separation, effect-modification strength, overlap, and sample size; measure reversal probability and bias relative to the same externally declared target, then reproduce the mechanism in a published two-sponsor MAIC case.
queue.priority_note: This is a good early experiment because the reversal is concrete and testable, provided it is framed as mapping when the known paradox occurs rather than rediscovering its remedy.

queue.title: Transitivity and conditional constancy cannot be tested in-sample
queue.answerable_part: A study can calibrate the power and specificity of a named falsification screen against prespecified violations, but no observed-data screen can verify transitivity or conditional constancy against all possible violations.
queue.design_sketch: Estimate whether a PAIC transport restriction is violated while varying omitted effect modification, covariate overlap, network size and compensating inconsistency. Evaluate dissimilarity screens, held-out contrast prediction and transported-control checks by type I error, power and the frequency with which each identifies the correct failure mechanism.
queue.priority_note: The impossibility claim itself is not a novel study, but calibrating one or two actionable screens is high priority and should precede attempts to assemble a broad diagnostic checklist.

queue.title: No agreed criterion for when a held-out-trial discrepancy falsifies
queue.answerable_part: A simulation can calibrate a particular held-out-trial discrepancy statistic and threshold under specified transport violations, but it cannot create a universally agreed falsification criterion across outcomes, estimands and network structures.
queue.design_sketch: Estimate the withheld trial's target-standardized treatment contrast while varying transport violation magnitude, network connectivity, heterogeneity, overlap and target-moment uncertainty. Compare standardized residual, predictive-tail probability and decision-scale discrepancy rules on type I error, power and coverage of the held-out contrast.
queue.priority_note: This is a clean and useful early experiment if restricted to identifiable leave-one-trial-out configurations rather than framed as a universal falsification standard.

queue.title: Missing aggregate summaries and unavailable IPD have no remedy
queue.answerable_part: A simulation can compare remedies for participant-level missingness in the IPD and test whether they preserve the transported estimand; it cannot create identification for wholly unreported target summaries or make unavailable study-level IPD recoverable.
queue.design_sketch: Estimate a target-population marginal treatment effect while varying covariate missingness from 5% to 50%, MAR versus controlled MNAR mechanisms, overlap, and whether missingness depends on effect modifiers. Compare complete-case MAIC, missingness-weighted MAIC, and transport-congenial multiple imputation using bias, interval coverage, and target-population discrepancy.
queue.priority_note: Run the bounded participant-level simulation early because it is tractable and informative, while explicitly excluding the structurally different absent-summary and unavailable-IPD layers.

queue.title: ESS is an insufficient overlap diagnostic and no battery is agreed
queue.answerable_part: A simulation can determine which candidate diagnostics add discrimination beyond ESS for consequential overlap failures, but it cannot create field-wide agreement on a standardized battery.
queue.design_sketch: Simulate a target-population marginal log odds ratio while varying convex-hull feasibility, tail overlap, omitted moments, effect modification and network redundancy. Compare ESS and candidate battery items by their sensitivity, specificity and area under the curve for detecting material bias or subnominal interval coverage.
queue.priority_note: Run an outcome-linked validation study early, but defer standard-setting until the useful diagnostics have been identified empirically.

queue.title: Outcome-model misspecification and doubly robust QBA
queue.answerable_part: A simulation can quantify the protection offered by augmented MAIC under combinations of measured-data model misspecification and explicit residual confounding, but it cannot establish robustness to every listed bias mechanism.
queue.design_sketch: Estimate a target marginal log odds ratio while varying misspecification of the weighting and outcome models, omitted-variable imbalance and treatment interaction; compare MAIC, outcome regression and cross-fitted augmented MAIC on bias, interval coverage and sensitivity-region coverage.
queue.priority_note: This is worth attempting early if restricted to one residual-bias model, because it can decisively separate double robustness from robustness to omitted variables.

queue.title: Survival pseudo-IPD reconstruction uncertainty is not propagated
queue.answerable_part: The study can quantify coverage loss from reconstruction error and the precision added by multiple reconstructions, but it cannot fully calibrate all pixel-reading and risk-table error distributions from one case.
queue.design_sketch: Simulate event data, render Kaplan-Meier curves and rounded risk tables, reconstruct pseudo-IPD repeatedly, and compare conditional versus ensemble analyses on bias and coverage of marginal survival and RMST contrasts. Reanalyze a published component comparison to measure how reconstruction propagation changes its interval width and conclusions.
queue.priority_note: The very high rating is defensible, but this should not run first because a credible simulation and nondecorative reanalysis require a reconstruction pipeline unlikely to fit into one week.

queue.title: Proportional or time-constant component effects may fail
queue.answerable_part: A simulation can evaluate time-varying component effects and RMST inference, but it cannot simultaneously settle cure, multistate, and long-term extrapolation models.
queue.design_sketch: Vary delayed, waning, and crossing component effects, follow-up length, and the amount of cross-subnetwork information, then compare proportional and time-varying component ML-NMR. Bias and coverage of target-population RMST differences and survival-probability contrasts decide whether the extension is adequate.
queue.priority_note: The scientific issue is important, but it should follow a usable marginal standardization path and be narrowed to time-varying effects rather than the full cure and multistate agenda.

queue.title: Missing data and MNAR sensitivity are unaddressed in component PAIC
queue.answerable_part: A study can evaluate a specified multiple-imputation and sensitivity workflow under selected MAR and MNAR mechanisms, but it cannot settle congeniality for every component model, missing variable type, and MNAR mechanism.
queue.design_sketch: Vary missingness fraction, covariate overlap, and MAR versus MNAR dependence in effect modifiers and outcomes, then compare complete-case analysis, imputation within each adjustment replicate, and a joint model. Bias, coverage, effective sample size, and tipping-point calibration for the target-population contrast are the deciding measures.
queue.priority_note: The very high rating reflects importance rather than study tractability; narrow it to one estimand, one missingness location, and one PAIC method before attempting it.

queue.title: No factorial study ranks which choice most often flips a decision
queue.answerable_part: A factorial study can rank coherent bridge, prior, and outcome-model choices within a fixed target estimand and scenario distribution; it cannot produce a universal ranking, and changing the target population cannot be treated as an ordinary estimator factor without changing the estimand.
queue.design_sketch: Hold a target-population incremental net-benefit estimand fixed and cross bridge assumptions, prior strength, and outcome-model form under varying overlap and effect modification. Use factorial contrasts in wrong-decision probability and recommendation reversals, analyzing alternative target populations separately as different decision questions.
queue.priority_note: Despite its very high rating, the unrestricted factorial would make a weak and potentially incoherent study; attempt it only after DEC-01 defines the decision metric and the factor set is reduced.

queue.title: No agreed ESS definition and no support-geometry diagnostics
queue.answerable_part: Simulation can compare whether proposed support-geometry diagnostics predict material estimation error; agreement on a universal ESS definition requires a separate standards process.
queue.design_sketch: Vary global overlap and localized support holes while holding conventional MAIC ESS approximately constant, then compare ESS, convex-hull distance, density-ratio and transport-cost diagnostics on discrimination and calibration for material error in the marginal treatment effect.
queue.priority_note: A narrowed comparison of support diagnostics is a strong early experiment, but the full proposed panel and cross-package standardization are too large for one study.

queue.title: QBA bias mechanisms are not crossed with the primary factors
queue.answerable_part: A designed simulation can determine conditional performance for selected interacting bias mechanisms, including misspecified and out-of-range sensitivity models, but cannot establish which mechanisms or sensitivity-parameter distributions are realistic in practice.
queue.design_sketch: Estimate an unanchored target-population marginal treatment effect while varying overlap, omitted-confounder strength, selection or censoring bias, dependence among sensitivity parameters, and whether the truth lies inside the elicited region. Compare QBA procedures on bias, coverage, false reassurance, decision reversal, and robustness when biases reinforce or cancel one another.
queue.priority_note: This is important but should follow a smaller classification-focused experiment because the proposed crossed design is large and otherwise risks becoming an uninformative scenario catalog.

queue.title: Transported control-arm outcomes are uncalibrated where it matters
queue.answerable_part: A hidden-truth reanalysis plus simulation can calibrate transported control-arm discrepancies for selected outcomes and bias mechanisms, but it cannot establish a universal acceptance tolerance or generalize across disease areas without a larger benchmark program.
queue.design_sketch: Estimate the target-population absolute control risk, survival curve or restricted mean survival time and the associated relative treatment effect. In simulations and a masked randomized-control reanalysis, vary prognostic transport bias, outcome-definition mismatch, censoring and care-context shifts, then assess discrepancy calibration, power to detect transport failure and relation to treatment-effect bias.
queue.priority_note: This is scientifically strong but not an early one-week study unless a suitable hidden-randomized-truth dataset is already analysis-ready.

queue.title: No criterion says when ML-NMR should be preferred to MAIC or STC
queue.answerable_part: A study can map settings in which ML-NMR has better statistical performance and demonstrate the corresponding diagnostic burden, but it cannot establish a universal default or settle every practical and normative tradeoff.
queue.design_sketch: Vary network connectivity, IPD availability, target-population information, effect-modifier overlap and outcome-model misspecification, then compare MAIC, STC and ML-NMR on bias, interval coverage, convergence and diagnostic detection for the target marginal treatment contrast. Reanalyze a published network in which the methods give materially different answers to test whether the simulation-derived criteria explain the difference.
queue.priority_note: Despite its very high rating, the universal question would make a weak study; an early project should narrow it to an explicit decision map over a few measurable design factors.

queue.title: Simulated-covariate QBA is an STC route, not a general solution
queue.answerable_part: A study can evaluate one or two extensions of simulated-covariate QBA, including whether MAIC remains feasible and calibrated, but cannot establish a general QBA solution for every weighting, one-stage and network estimator.
queue.design_sketch: For a target marginal log odds ratio, vary omitted-covariate prevalence, correlation with measured modifiers, treatment interaction and source-target transport error; compare STC and sensitivity-adjusted MAIC on bias, coverage, effective sample size and calibration failure.
queue.priority_note: Despite its very high rating, this is a weak single-study target unless narrowed to a direct STC-versus-MAIC experiment with explicit assumptions.

queue.title: Total bias is non-additive, so one-at-a-time analyses mislead
queue.answerable_part: A study can demonstrate and quantify nonadditivity for a prespecified combination of population, confounding and measurement biases, but it cannot define a universal joint-bias region or cover all mechanisms.
queue.design_sketch: For a target marginal risk ratio or RMST, jointly vary effect-modifier imbalance, omitted confounding and outcome misclassification under positive and negative dependence; compare simultaneous adjustment with one-at-a-time and sequential corrections on total bias, coverage and decision reversals.
queue.priority_note: A two-bias or three-bias factorial experiment would be decisive and useful, but the unrestricted catalog problem is too broad to attempt early as one study.

queue.title: Survival QBA beyond the hazard ratio with limited aggregate data
queue.answerable_part: A study could settle performance for one or two prespecified functionals, such as RMST difference and landmark survival, under aggregate or reconstructed comparator data; it could not settle cure, competing-risk, recurrent-event and multistate QBA simultaneously.
queue.design_sketch: Estimate target-population RMST differences and landmark survival under unmeasured prognostic imbalance, varying overlap, censoring, baseline-hazard shape and Kaplan-Meier reconstruction error. Compare bias, interval coverage and tipping-point recovery for curve-based and pseudo-IPD implementations, followed by a published unanchored PAIC reanalysis.
queue.priority_note: Run an RMST-focused version early because it is decision-relevant and testable, but defer the entry's full multi-endpoint agenda.

queue.title: maicplus variance, trimming and estimand disclosure gaps
queue.answerable_part: A study can compare joint-sandwich, fixed-weight and bootstrap variance estimators and quantify trimming trade-offs, but it cannot simultaneously settle reporting metadata, parallelization and the normative choice of a trimming rule.
queue.design_sketch: Estimate the target-population marginal treatment effect while varying effective sample size, overlap, outcome prevalence and weight truncation; compare bias, interval coverage, variance-estimation error, calibration loss and the divergence between the nominal and post-trimming target populations.
queue.priority_note: Despite its very high rating, this is too bundled for one study; the variance comparison is the cleanest early experiment, while trimming requires an explicitly defined post-trimming estimand.

queue.title: Unreleased cpaic has no tracked simulation benchmark or replication
queue.answerable_part: One study can deliver a reproducible adversarial benchmark and a real-data reanalysis, but it cannot supply independent replication of an author-developed method or establish robustness beyond the chosen violations.
queue.design_sketch: Estimate a target-population treatment contrast while varying additivity violations, treatment-by-component interactions, overlap, target misspecification and bridge failure. Compare component ML-NMR with MAIC and non-component alternatives on bias, coverage, failure rate and Monte Carlo error, then test whether conclusions persist in a full-IPD worked example.
queue.priority_note: The catalog rating is justified, but the full proposal is too large for an early one-week study; a preregistered adversarial simulation module would be the strongest first increment.

queue.title: Held-out IPD is not used to benchmark transport against truth
queue.answerable_part: Masked-IPD analysis can measure discrepancy from a prespecified full-IPD reference analysis of the same estimand, but the reference is uncertain rather than truth and one dataset cannot establish general transport validity.
queue.design_sketch: Mask each selected trial to published aggregate summaries, estimate its target-population marginal treatment effect using each PAIC method, and compare it with a full-IPD standardized analysis targeting the identical population and effect scale. Use uncertainty-aware discrepancy, arm-level prediction error, interval agreement, and decision agreement as performance measures.
queue.priority_note: This would be a strong benchmark but should run only after an appropriate shared multi-trial IPD dataset is secured, making it a poor first study despite its scientific value.

queue.title: No curated benchmark validates bridged cross-gap comparisons
queue.answerable_part: A study can create and independently analyze a small benchmark of connected networks with deleted links, but establishing a representative, reusable benchmark with full-IPD gold standards requires substantial data access and curation beyond one study week.
queue.design_sketch: Estimate target-standardized cross-gap treatment contrasts after deleting observed network links from connected datasets. Vary which link is removed and the population and design separation across the induced gap, then measure bias, interval coverage and decision agreement against the retained direct or full-network estimate.
queue.priority_note: The benchmark would be valuable, but it should not run early unless suitable IPD datasets and permissions are already secured because curation, not analysis, is the binding task.

queue.title: Component PAIC needs joint population-and-bridge bias analysis
queue.answerable_part: A simulation can quantify reinforcement and cancellation between population-transport and component-bridge bias in a specified component ML-NMR model; it cannot settle defensible joint parameter regions or all listed bias mechanisms.
queue.design_sketch: Estimate a target marginal log odds ratio or RMST while jointly varying omitted-modifier imbalance, component main-effect drift, component-by-modifier drift and their dependence; compare joint versus one-at-a-time analyses on bias, coverage and decision reversals.
queue.priority_note: Although highly rated, this is too expansive for an early study and should follow work on target-law uncertainty and multivariate sensitivity dependence.

queue.title: Pseudo-IPD cannot express delayed entry or assessment windows
queue.answerable_part: A simulation can quantify bias from treating delayed entry and interval-censored assessments as exactly observed right-censored data; it cannot reconstruct entry times or assessment intervals that publications never report.
queue.design_sketch: Estimate target RMST and event risk at a common horizon while varying delayed-entry dependence, assessment-grid spacing, between-trial follow-up differences, and effect-modifier overlap. Compare analyses using the true observation process with standard reconstructed pseudo-IPD on bias, coverage, and survival-curve calibration.
queue.priority_note: Despite its high rating, this is best treated as a focused sensitivity benchmark because the central missing-information claim is already logically clear and cannot be solved by a better reconstruction algorithm.

queue.title: Flexible outcome surfaces and support diagnostics in standardization
queue.answerable_part: A simulation can determine when flexible outcome surfaces and proposed support diagnostics improve estimation under specified data-generating mechanisms, but cannot establish universal out-of-support validity or identify causal effect modifiers from fitted interactions.
queue.design_sketch: Estimate a target-population marginal log odds ratio while varying modifier overlap from 0.9 to 0.2, outcome-surface nonlinearity, interaction strength and target density-ratio estimation error. Compare parametric STC or ML-NMR with BART and Gaussian-process standardization on bias and interval coverage, and compare support diagnostics on sensitivity and false-positive rate for unsupported target profiles.
queue.priority_note: This deserves an early run because it supports a clean known-truth experiment, although the BART, Gaussian-process and weighted-conformal components should be narrowed to one primary comparison.

queue.title: Target joint covariate distribution is only approximately known
queue.answerable_part: A simulation can quantify bias and undercoverage from Gaussian-copula misspecification and assess sensitivity envelopes, but it cannot identify the unknown joint distribution in a real target population from marginal summaries alone.
queue.design_sketch: Hold reported margins and rank correlation fixed while varying the true copula across Gaussian, asymmetric, and tail-dependent families and varying outcome-model nonlinearity. Compare standardized contrasts under Gaussian reconstruction, flexible copulas, and sensitivity envelopes using bias, coverage, and envelope containment of the true estimand.
queue.priority_note: Important but broad; begin with the copula-misspecification experiment and defer posterior reconstruction uncertainty and robust partial identification to later studies.

queue.title: Unreleased cpaic shares one tau and one IPD-row residual variance
queue.answerable_part: A simulation can identify when shared heterogeneity and residual scales materially distort inference and when structured alternatives are estimable, but it cannot select a universally appropriate heterogeneity structure.
queue.design_sketch: Vary component- or subnetwork-specific heterogeneity, study-specific residual variance, network sparsity, and the number of IPD studies. Compare shared, stratified, and hierarchically shrunk tau and sigma models on treatment-effect bias, interval coverage, variance-component recovery, and prior sensitivity.
queue.priority_note: A useful second-wave study, but the unreleased implementation and the many candidate variance structures make it less decisive than the covariance and shared-Gamma problems.

queue.title: No evidence on how the modifier set changes across effect scales
queue.answerable_part: A study can show how estimand-specific oracle or prespecified adjustment sets and conclusions change across effect scales in defined scenarios and a real reanalysis, but cannot estimate how often appraisals change across the field from one case.
queue.design_sketch: Generate binary or time-to-event outcomes with prognostic and conditional interaction effects, then derive and fit scale-specific adjustment sets for risk difference, risk ratio, odds ratio and hazard-ratio estimands as applicable. Compare modifier-set overlap, contrast bias, coverage and decision reversals, followed by the same scale-sensitivity analysis in a published PAIC dataset.
queue.priority_note: Although rated below covariate selection, this is the cleaner early experiment because the scale-specific estimands and decision-reversal criterion can be prespecified precisely.

queue.title: Measurement non-equivalence of covariates across trials
queue.answerable_part: Simulation can quantify how specified measurement errors and crosswalk uncertainty affect PAIC estimates and whether correction or sensitivity procedures cover the truth; it cannot identify the latent target distribution when no bridge information or mapping assumptions exist.
queue.design_sketch: Estimate a target-population marginal treatment effect while varying source-versus-target calibration shifts, reliability, cut-point misclassification, interaction strength, and availability of a bridge sample. Compare naive adjustment, measurement-error correction, harmonization, and sensitivity intervals on bias, coverage, and decision reversals.
queue.priority_note: A lower-complexity simulation is a clean and useful early study, provided it reports nonidentification rather than presenting correction without bridge information as universally available.

queue.title: Data access is simulated as benign rather than informative
queue.answerable_part: One study can isolate a small number of access mechanisms, such as sampling error in target summaries or informative censoring, but cannot settle the entire collection of availability, reporting, missingness, reconstruction, and follow-up mechanisms.
queue.design_sketch: For a marginal target-population treatment effect, vary target-summary sample size and informative censoring strength while holding overlap and outcome-model correctness fixed, then measure bias, interval coverage, and decision error for PAIC estimators that either ignore or propagate those uncertainties. A second factor can make IPD availability depend on an effect-relevant study characteristic to quantify selection over studies.
queue.priority_note: The target-summary uncertainty experiment deserves an early run because it is simple and commonly ignored; the full access-mechanism program is too broad for one early study.

queue.title: Treatment hierarchies lack a declared target-population referent
queue.answerable_part: A study can define target-standardized ranking functionals and quantify how target-population uncertainty and covariate shifts change ranks, but it cannot establish journal or HTA reporting requirements.
queue.design_sketch: Estimate marginal relative effects and SUCRA or probability-best values for several declared target covariate distributions, varying effect-modifier imbalance and uncertainty in target moments; assess rank reversals, rank coverage, and decision changes, then reproduce the analysis in a published IPD-plus-aggregate network.
queue.priority_note: Run early because it yields a visible, decision-relevant population-adjustment result, although the reporting-standard component requires later consensus work.

queue.title: Node splitting compares paths without standardizing to a target
queue.answerable_part: A simulation can quantify false flags and masked inconsistency from population mismatch and compare conditional with target-marginalized node splitting; it will not settle the broader construction of population-indexed inconsistency models.
queue.design_sketch: Estimate a target-marginal inconsistency factor while varying covariate-distribution separation between direct and indirect paths, effect-modification strength and the presence or absence of true loop inconsistency. Compare unadjusted and ML-NMR-adjusted node splitting on type I error, power, bias and interval coverage.
queue.priority_note: This deserves an early run because it is a focused experiment with a clear decision consequence: whether ordinary node splitting materially misdiagnoses population mismatch.

queue.title: No robustness theory for censoring-weighted survival transport
queue.answerable_part: A Monte Carlo study can characterize TADA under heavy censoring, weak overlap, censoring-model misspecification, and nonproportional censoring hazards, including variance-estimator coverage; it cannot establish robustness to unmeasured informative censoring or supply doubly robust theory.
queue.design_sketch: Target the transported marginal log hazard ratio while varying censoring from 10% to 70%, covariate overlap, proportional versus time-varying censoring hazards, and misspecification of the participation and censoring models. Compare bias, empirical standard error, bootstrap or sandwich standard-error calibration, and 95% interval coverage.
queue.priority_note: This deserves an early run because the estimator exists and the disputed operating characteristics form a clean simulation question, although doubly robust extension should be a separate project.

queue.title: Overdispersed counts and recurrent events as total disease burden
queue.answerable_part: A simulation can quantify when Poisson-based PAIC retains an approximately unbiased rate ratio but loses interval coverage, and when zero-process, exposure, frailty, or conditional-mean misspecification creates transport bias; it cannot also settle the broader recurrent-event methodology program.
queue.design_sketch: Estimate the target-population rate ratio while varying negative-binomial dispersion, structural-zero prevalence, covariate-dependent exposure, frailty heterogeneity, and covariate overlap. Compare weighted Poisson MAIC and Poisson ML-NMR with correctly specified count models on bias, interval coverage, RMSE, and target absolute-rate calibration.
queue.priority_note: Run the focused count-outcome benchmark early, but separate it from recurrent-event and joint-frailty development, which would make the nominally high-priority problem too broad for one study.

queue.title: Proportional odds, category probabilities, and ordinal utilities
queue.answerable_part: A simulation can determine when proportional-odds ML-NMR gives misleading target category probabilities and whether partial proportional-odds or alternative ordinal links materially improve estimation; preference elicitation and utility transport require separate studies.
queue.design_sketch: Estimate target-standardized category probabilities and expected ordinal utility while varying threshold-specific treatment effects, effect-modifier overlap, category sparsity, and utility uncertainty. Compare proportional-odds, partial proportional-odds, adjacent-category, and continuation-ratio ML-NMR on probability bias, interval coverage, calibration, and decision loss.
queue.priority_note: The ordinal-model benchmark is a clean and useful experiment, but the catalog's high rating overstates the urgency because proportional-odds ML-NMR and standardized category probabilities already exist.

queue.title: Reconstruction uncertainty from digitized Kaplan-Meier curves
queue.answerable_part: The study can quantify how calibrated Kaplan-Meier reconstruction uncertainty propagates into target RMST, survival probabilities, and extrapolation; constructing and validating a complete Bayesian observation model for every digitization and reporting process is a larger problem.
queue.design_sketch: Estimate target RMST and milestone survival after reconstructing pseudo-IPD while varying image resolution, rounding, censoring patterns, risk-table granularity, overlap, and reconstruction calibration. Measure bias and coverage against known simulated IPD, then reanalyze a published PAIC to determine whether reconstruction variability changes its conclusion.
queue.priority_note: Run this relatively early because existing ensemble reconstruction makes a concrete simulation-plus-reanalysis possible without first inventing a new survival estimator.

queue.title: No standardized sample-size planning guidance or software for PAIC
queue.answerable_part: A study can produce calibrated planning rules for specified methods, estimands and outcome types, but not one universal sample-size rule for all PAIC designs.
queue.design_sketch: For a target marginal log odds ratio or restricted mean survival-time difference, vary nominal sample size, event count, overlap, modifier dimension and treatment allocation. Compare planned and achieved power, confidence-interval width and coverage using influence-function and simulation-based calculations.
queue.priority_note: A tightly scoped binary-outcome or survival planning study is a clean, useful early project even though universal guidance is too broad for one paper.

queue.title: Benchmarking and negative controls as data-based calibration
queue.answerable_part: Simulation can determine when held-out benchmarks or negative controls detect consequential residual bias and how misleading calibration by analogy can be; it cannot show that such controls bound unmeasured bias without additional assumptions.
queue.design_sketch: Estimate the marginal treatment effect after unanchored adjustment while varying the strength, prevalence, correlation and dimensionality of omitted prognostic factors and the validity of a negative control. Compare diagnostic sensitivity, specificity and calibration of inferred bias ranges against the known residual bias.
queue.priority_note: This lower-rated problem is a strong early simulation because it has clear truth, measurable diagnostic performance and an important negative result if calibration fails.

queue.title: drMAIC has no methods paper and no independent evaluation
queue.answerable_part: A simulation can test the implementation and finite-sample double-robust behavior when either nuisance model is correct, but the double-robustness theorem itself requires an analytic derivation and real-data exchangeability remains untestable.
queue.design_sketch: Estimate the marginal target-population treatment effect while crossing correct and misspecified weighting and outcome models with strong versus weak overlap; compare drMAIC, conventional MAIC, G-MAIC and g-computation on bias, coverage, interval width and failed-fit frequency.
queue.priority_note: This is a clean and comparatively decisive early benchmark because the required factorial design follows directly from the package's central claim.

queue.title: Privacy guarantees and governance for shared trial-level data
queue.answerable_part: A simulation can determine privacy-budget and sample-size combinations that preserve useful target moments, and can evaluate uncertainty propagation through specified PAIC estimators; it cannot settle cross-sponsor governance conventions.
queue.design_sketch: Estimate a target-population marginal treatment effect while varying arm size, privacy budget, moment dimension, covariate overlap, and release mechanism. Compare bias, interval coverage, effective sample size, and utility against non-private analyses and analyses that incorrectly treat privatized moments as fixed.
queue.priority_note: Run the estimator-and-privacy simulation early after narrowing the scope, but separate the governance question into a standards project.

queue.title: Selection uncertainty in PAIC interaction shrinkage is uncalibrated
queue.answerable_part: A focused study can compare whole-procedure interval coverage for a small set of interaction-shrinkage and selection methods, but cannot settle the full catalog of priors, heredity rules, selection algorithms, and network structures at once.
queue.design_sketch: Estimate target-population treatment effects while varying the number, sparsity, and strength of true treatment-by-covariate interactions, network information, and overlap. Compare a prespecified regularized horseshoe, hierarchy-respecting shrinkage, projection selection, and an all-interactions model on bias, coverage after selection, interval width, and false interaction discoveries.
queue.priority_note: The calibration question is important, but the proposed benchmark is too large for an early study; run a sharply reduced comparison first.

queue.title: Scenario grids omit network topology and information placement
queue.answerable_part: A study can estimate how selected topology and IPD-placement factors affect specified PAIC estimators and contrasts, but it cannot support conclusions over the unrestricted space of network structures.
queue.design_sketch: Generate chain, star, loop-rich and articulation-edge networks with fixed total outcome information, vary which studies provide IPD, and compare bias, coverage, estimability and decision error for a prespecified target-population contrast.
queue.priority_note: Run after simpler two-study failure-signature work because it is important but computationally and interpretively larger, and its conclusions will be topology-family specific.

queue.title: Multi-arm covariance is lost when contrasts are adjusted pairwise
queue.answerable_part: A simulation can determine whether joint arm-level weighting and a multivariate bootstrap recover the covariance and interval coverage of weighted multi-arm contrasts, but deriving and productionizing a generally valid estimator is a larger methodological project.
queue.design_sketch: Estimate target-population log treatment contrasts and their joint covariance after applying one MAIC weight set to three-arm and four-arm IPD trials. Vary arm sizes, weight instability, outcome correlation and variance imbalance, then compare naive pairwise, sandwich and re-estimated multivariate-bootstrap procedures on covariance bias and simultaneous interval coverage.
queue.priority_note: This is a valuable but technically substantial project, and an early study should first benchmark the multivariate bootstrap rather than promise a complete arm-level MAIC framework in one step.

queue.title: No calibrated small-study interval method for population-adjusted NMA
queue.answerable_part: One study can quantify undercoverage and determine whether candidate bootstrap or Bayesian interval procedures are adequately calibrated over a prespecified design region; it cannot deliver an exact or universally calibrated small-sample method for every population-adjusted network.
queue.design_sketch: Vary the number of studies from 2 to 16, the number of IPD studies, covariate overlap, heterogeneity, and effect-modifier strength; compare MAIC/STC network intervals and ML-NMR credible intervals, including a study-level bootstrap that re-estimates weights, on 95% coverage and interval width for the target-population relative effect.
queue.priority_note: This deserves an early slot because it is a direct PAIC inference problem with a decisive coverage endpoint, although the full proposed calibration is closer to a month-long study than a one-week experiment.

queue.title: No principled basis for shared effect-modifier treatment classes
queue.answerable_part: A study can quantify estimator sensitivity and evaluate prespecified partition-selection rules, but it cannot establish that clinically dissimilar treatments truly share an interaction vector when those interactions are not separately identified.
queue.design_sketch: Vary within-class interaction heterogeneity, separation between true classes, covariate overlap, and network information while comparing candidate partitions on bias and coverage of the target marginal contrast; in real applications, refit every clinically defensible partition and report the resulting contrast range.
queue.priority_note: This is central to population adjustment, but the full selection problem is too broad for an early one-week study; begin with a decisive partition-sensitivity analysis.

queue.title: Model and bridge selection uncertainty never enters the interval
queue.answerable_part: A simulation can quantify coverage after a specified model-selection procedure and test model averaging or repeated-selection resampling; it cannot empirically choose among observationally equivalent identification bridges.
queue.design_sketch: Target a population-adjusted marginal treatment effect while varying the true modifier set, overlap, candidate-model multiplicity, and whether selection occurs at the patient, contrast, or study level. Compare naive conditional intervals, bootstrap procedures repeating selection, Bayesian model averaging, and stacking using coverage, interval width, and predictive loss at the declared unit.
queue.priority_note: The question is important but should follow simpler uncertainty studies because a credible design must first restrict the candidate models and prediction unit rather than testing every selection and bridge problem together.

queue.title: No post-selection inference for model choice in population adjustment
queue.answerable_part: A bounded study can evaluate post-selection coverage for a prespecified modifier-selection or tuning workflow and compare feasible corrections; it cannot settle selective inference for every PAIC model class or uncertainty about scientifically chosen prior scales.
queue.design_sketch: Target a transported marginal treatment effect while varying modifier sparsity, signal strength, overlap, sample size, and selection by information criterion or cross-validation. Compare intervals conditional on the selected model with repeated-selection bootstrap, shrinkage with full posterior propagation, model averaging, and sample splitting using coverage and interval width.
queue.priority_note: This is substantively important but overlaps heavily with MIS-04 and should be combined with it or delayed until one concrete selection workflow is chosen.

queue.title: No support diagnostic aggregates over a PAIC target distribution
queue.answerable_part: A study can validate specified target-aggregated support measures under selected outcome models, but cannot establish a universal diagnostic or abstention threshold when the target joint distribution is unidentified.
queue.design_sketch: Estimate a target-standardized marginal log odds ratio while varying source-to-target support, target profiles and alternative joint distributions sharing the same published moments. Compare aggregated distance, hull, density, leverage and prediction-variance measures by their ability to predict bias, undercoverage and failed extrapolation.
queue.priority_note: This is important but should follow simpler diagnostic work because reconstructing the target distribution is itself an unresolved source of sensitivity.

queue.title: No agreed leave-one-out unit for mixed IPD and aggregate likelihoods
queue.answerable_part: A study can define and compare patient-, arm- and study-level predictive targets and determine when approximate LOO fails for each; it cannot establish one universally correct held-out unit because the appropriate unit depends on the prediction question.
queue.design_sketch: Estimate out-of-sample predictive accuracy for new patients, arms and studies while varying IPD proportion, study heterogeneity, leverage and aggregate-data contribution. Compare grouped PSIS-LOO with exact refits on bias in expected log predictive density, Pareto-k failure and model-selection accuracy, then examine the distinctions in a mixed IPD and aggregate ML-NMR case.
queue.priority_note: This is a clean methodological study if reframed around distinct predictive estimands rather than searching for one agreed unit, but exact refits make it slower than an early quick win.

queue.title: outstandR is pairwise only with no network or disconnected validation
queue.answerable_part: Simulation and reanalysis can characterize sensitivity to outcome-model misspecification and target-distribution reconstruction; they cannot validate an unidentified bridge across a genuinely disconnected network.
queue.design_sketch: Estimate a marginal target-population treatment effect while varying covariate-distribution reconstruction, effect-modifier overlap, outcome-model misspecification and network connectivity; compare bias, coverage and estimate movement, then reproduce the most consequential sensitivity in a published limited-IPD comparison.
queue.priority_note: Run a focused pairwise robustness study early, but defer disconnected-network extension until its bridge assumptions and identification conditions are stated analytically.

queue.title: cpaic and mlumr are unreleased and independently unvalidated
queue.answerable_part: Independent work can evaluate implementation accuracy and finite-sample behavior under specified structural violations, but it cannot empirically validate component additivity, bridge exchangeability or unanchored conditional exchangeability in applications where those assumptions are untestable.
queue.design_sketch: Estimate target-population component and absolute treatment effects while varying overlap, omitted prognostic and effect-modifying covariates, component interactions and bridge strength; compare bias, coverage, convergence and sensitivity-analysis calibration, then independently reproduce one published example for each package.
queue.priority_note: Independent validation deserves early attention, but the catalog entry is too broad for one week and should be split into a focused cpaic benchmark and a separate ML-UMR benchmark.

queue.title: Match acceptance thresholds are uncalibrated against bridge bias
queue.answerable_part: A study can estimate bias, coverage, and decision-reversal curves for specified dissimilarity indices and clinical domains, but it cannot establish a universally transferable acceptance threshold.
queue.design_sketch: Estimate the cross-gap treatment contrast after deleting known edges from connected networks; vary the match threshold, overlap, covariate weighting, and index normalization, and compare NMI estimates with the full-network result on bias, interval coverage, edge retention, and decision reversal. Monte Carlo networks should establish operating characteristics, while real-network deletions test whether the calibration survives realistic covariate reporting and topology.
queue.priority_note: Run early only after fixing the dissimilarity index; the high rating is justified, but a study claiming one universal cutoff would be weak.

queue.title: Data-driven modifier and causal-structure discovery with few trials
queue.answerable_part: A simulation can estimate how many trials, events and target observations are needed for stable modifier discovery and target standardization, but cannot show that a learned adjustment set is causally sufficient in practice.
queue.design_sketch: Estimate the marginal treatment effect in an external target while varying the number of trials, events per arm, overlap, modifier sparsity, nonlinear interactions and study-level confounding. Compare multi-study causal forests with prespecified STC or ML-NMR on target-effect bias and coverage, modifier-selection stability and false discovery of noncausal interactions.
queue.priority_note: This is a feasible but secondary simulation and should follow studies of prespecified modifiers and support because discovery cannot repair unidentified transport bias.

queue.title: Flexible interaction surfaces inside network evidence synthesis
queue.answerable_part: A study can evaluate one implementable flexible interaction model, such as BART or a Gaussian process, but cannot settle both model classes, computational design and causal effect-modifier discovery at once.
queue.design_sketch: Vary interaction nonlinearity, source-target overlap and the proportion of the target population outside observed support, then compare a flexible-surface ML-NMR with parametric ML-NMR on bias, interval coverage and computation for the target marginal effect. Also measure whether a support diagnostic discriminates scenarios with unacceptable extrapolation error.
queue.priority_note: This is promising but should follow simpler work on overlap and extrapolation diagnostics because flexibility cannot solve absent support.

queue.title: No mixture-over-populations model transports to a declared target
queue.answerable_part: A study can evaluate a finite-mixture or Dirichlet-process transport model under specified heterogeneity and prior classes; the separate safe-Bayes learning-rate problem is too broad to settle simultaneously.
queue.design_sketch: Vary the number and separation of latent study-population clusters, IPD availability, target overlap and prior concentration, then compare mixture and conventional hierarchical transport models on bias, coverage, predictive accuracy and prior-to-posterior movement for the target contrast.
queue.priority_note: The entry bundles two difficult developments, so it should not run early unless narrowed to one mixture model and one transported estimand.

queue.title: ML-NMR integration cost is unaddressed for flexible survival models
queue.answerable_part: A study can quantify the runtime-accuracy frontier for a prespecified subset of acceleration methods and survival models, but cannot settle every proposed backend, likelihood and unified diagnostic at once.
queue.design_sketch: Estimate marginal survival contrasts while varying integration points, covariate dimension, number of aggregate studies, censoring and baseline-hazard flexibility. Benchmark selected approximations against a high-accuracy ML-NMR reference using runtime, likelihood error, contrast bias, interval coverage and predictive log score.
queue.priority_note: Important but too expansive for an early study; begin with a focused benchmark of integration-point adaptation and within-chain parallelization.

queue.title: Representation learning for low-dimensional population encodings
queue.answerable_part: A study can identify when a specified representation objective preserves known effect modification and transport performance, but cannot establish that data-driven compression preserves unknown effect modifiers generally.
queue.design_sketch: Estimate marginal target-population treatment effects while varying representation dimension, modifier sparsity, nonlinear heterogeneity, measurement shifts, and population overlap. Compare learned encodings with declared mappings on treatment-effect bias, interval coverage, interaction preservation, reconstruction diagnostics, and performance in a real biomarker-harmonization example.
queue.priority_note: Do not run early: it is interesting but speculative, computationally substantial, and incapable of resolving the central unknown-modifier objection.

queue.title: Method evaluations score estimator error, not decision error
queue.design_sketch: Estimate treatment-specific target-population net benefit and the resulting treatment recommendation while varying overlap, effect modification, decision threshold, and loss asymmetry. Compare PAIC methods on bias and coverage as well as wrong-decision probability, net-benefit error, and rank reversal to determine whether estimator and decision rankings disagree.
queue.priority_note: This is a clean, decisive early experiment with modest implementation cost, although its conclusions must remain conditional on the prespecified decision model and thresholds.

queue.title: No calibrated rule says when within- and across-trial interactions may be pooled
queue.design_sketch: Vary the ecological bias between within- and across-trial interaction estimates, number of trials, dispersion of trial covariate means, and overlap; compare pooling rules on null rejection rate, power, and coverage of the pooled treatment-covariate interaction.
queue.priority_note: This is a clean and decisive simulation with direct implications for ML-NMR and is a strong early candidate.

queue.title: Predictive criteria and population comparison cannot validate a bridge
queue.answerable_part: Simulation can determine whether proposed diagnostics discriminate valid from invalid transport or bridge models under specified violations, but no observed-covariate diagnostic can rule out arbitrary unmeasured effect modification.
queue.design_sketch: Vary measured and unmeasured effect-modifier imbalance, overlap, and bridge misspecification while targeting a marginal treatment effect in a held-out population. Compare ordinary predictive criteria, covariate-balance checks, leave-one-study validation, and synthetic-link deletion by their ability to rank models according to cross-population bias and interval coverage.
queue.priority_note: This deserves an early experiment because it is a clean diagnostic-discrimination question with direct consequences for every PAIC family.

queue.title: Negative controls for ITC lack catalogues, power and calibration
queue.answerable_part: A simulation can characterize the power and specificity of specified negative-control tests for cross-study transport bias, but it cannot establish disease-specific catalogues or validate the substantive null and shared-bias assumptions of proposed controls.
queue.design_sketch: Estimate whether a population-adjusted contrast is affected by residual transport bias while varying control-outcome prevalence, correlation with the primary outcome, shared-bias strength, covariate correlation and network size. Evaluate negative-control tests and empirical calibration on type I error, power and coverage of the primary contrast.
queue.priority_note: The power study is feasible, but this should follow more direct diagnostics because unavailable outcomes and questionable control validity may limit its practical payoff regardless of statistical calibration.

queue.title: Strict component additivity may be clinically false
queue.answerable_part: A simulation can compare prespecified shrinkage strategies and quantify the bias from omitted interactions for selected component-PAIC designs, but it cannot determine whether additivity is clinically true across applications.
queue.design_sketch: Estimate target-population cross-gap regimen contrasts while varying interaction magnitude, hierarchy, sparsity, observed component combinations, covariate overlap, and subnetwork drift. Compare additive, prespecified-interaction, and heredity-constrained models on bias, coverage, interval width, and the frequency with which likelihood information rather than shrinkage determines the contrast.
queue.priority_note: The PAIC-specific portion is important but too broad for an early one-week study; first narrow it to omitted-interaction sensitivity for one outcome family and network design.

queue.title: Informative censoring and outcome-dependent missingness
queue.answerable_part: A simulation can evaluate transport-congenial imputation, censoring weighting and joint models under specified missingness mechanisms; it cannot determine an unidentified outcome-dependent mechanism from observed trial data alone.
queue.design_sketch: Vary source-versus-comparator censoring prevalence, dependence on latent outcomes, availability of time-varying predictors and target overlap, then compare naive PAIC, transport-congenial IPCW or imputation and joint models on bias and interval coverage of the target survival or mean contrast.
queue.priority_note: The clinical importance supports high priority, but the entry is too broad for an early one-week study and should first be narrowed to one outcome type and one sensitivity parameterization.

queue.title: Measurement and misclassification QBA under population adjustment
queue.answerable_part: A simulation can validate a joint measurement-error and population-adjustment estimator for a selected error mechanism and outcome, but cannot resolve the external validity of the required validation data or cover all measurement mechanisms.
queue.design_sketch: Estimate a target marginal risk ratio while varying binary sensitivity and specificity, continuous calibration error, validation-sample size, source-target overlap and whether the error affects a balancing covariate or outcome. Compare naive, sequential and joint models on bias, interval coverage and interval width.
queue.priority_note: This is valuable but too large for an early one-week study unless restricted to one misclassified binary covariate and one outcome type.

queue.title: Propagating every uncertainty layer without prohibitive cost
queue.answerable_part: A computational study can compare coverage, failure rates and cost for a defined subset of propagation schemes and uncertainty layers; it cannot settle a universal inventory or optimal scheme for every PAIC estimator.
queue.design_sketch: For an unanchored target marginal treatment effect, vary overlap, sensitivity-grid size, target-law uncertainty and numerical integration accuracy; compare nested bootstrap, parametric bootstrap and modular Monte Carlo on interval coverage, Monte Carlo error, failed-replicate rates and runtime.
queue.priority_note: This should follow estimator-specific QBA work because a narrowly defined propagation benchmark is useful, whereas propagating every conceivable layer is not a coherent early study.

queue.title: No curated public suite for bridge-deletion validation with IPD
queue.answerable_part: A study can create and analyze one or several valid deletion benchmarks for PAIC, but it cannot establish a maintained public suite or general method validity, and suitable public multi-trial IPD may not exist.
queue.design_sketch: In connected datasets with compatible IPD or reconstructed pseudo-IPD, delete an eligible randomized link while preserving estimability, target each method to the held-out trial population, and compare reconstructed marginal effects and treatment decisions with the held-out randomized estimate. Stratify discrepancies by covariate overlap and reliance on extrapolation.
queue.priority_note: Although highly rated, this should not run early because data curation and estimand harmonization dominate the work and a single deletion supplies weak general evidence.

queue.title: No prospectively blinded calibration program for PAIC and QBA
