queue.answerable_part: A blinded randomized-benchmark exercise can estimate calibration performance in one defined clinical and data setting, but one exercise cannot establish transportable calibration across diseases and bias mechanisms.
queue.design_sketch: Use a concealed randomized control result as the reference estimand and have analysts estimate the same target-population hazard ratio or restricted mean survival-time difference using an external comparator and prespecified QBA. Measure absolute discrepancy, interval coverage and whether tipping conclusions agree with the revealed randomized result.
queue.priority_note: Despite its very high rating, this should not run early without committed access to masked randomized and external-control IPD because data governance, not statistical design, is the binding constraint.

queue.title: Decision QBA: net benefit, tipping surfaces and extrapolation
queue.answerable_part: A study could evaluate shared-draw propagation of PAIC bias through one survival and economic model, but could not establish a generally adequate framework across diseases, extrapolation families and decision rules.
queue.design_sketch: Estimate incremental net benefit under residual treatment-effect bias, varying bias magnitude, bias dependence, survival extrapolation family and willingness-to-pay threshold. Measure decision-reversal probability, expected regret and coverage of the true net benefit, then reproduce the workflow in an actual HTA model.
queue.priority_note: The decision endpoint is important, but this should follow a narrower estimand-scale QBA because otherwise the economic model merely inherits an unsettled bias specification.

queue.title: Cross-environment invariance as a screen for bridges and modifiers
queue.answerable_part: A simulation can measure whether an invariance screen detects unstable modifiers or bridges where instability is observable, but no screen can confirm validity across an unobserved gap.
queue.design_sketch: Estimate a target-population treatment contrast while varying the number of trial environments, event counts, genuine modifier drift, measurement shifts and non-collapsibility-induced apparent instability. Evaluate the screen's sensitivity, specificity and abstention rate for bridge violations, together with bias and coverage after flagged bridges are routed to sensitivity analysis.
queue.priority_note: This is a clean early diagnostic experiment if framed as falsification rather than validation, despite having lower program relevance than core PAIC estimators.

queue.title: IPD availability may be informative rather than random
queue.answerable_part: A simulation can evaluate robustness checks and observed-characteristic selection models, but it cannot identify selection on unavailable individual-level characteristics or determine the real-world selection mechanism.
queue.design_sketch: Vary the proportion of trials supplying IPD and the strength of selection based on observed trial variables versus latent effect modification, then compare naive analysis, observed-variable selection adjustment, and grouped leave-IPD-out diagnostics. Bias and coverage of target effects, plus the diagnostic's ability to flag influential IPD subsets, decide the answerable part.
queue.priority_note: Useful as a sensitivity-method study, but it should follow more identifiable problems because no internal analysis can resolve selection on unobserved IPD quantities.

queue.title: Effect-modifier selection does not check interaction consistency
queue.answerable_part: A simulation can establish the operating characteristics of interaction-consistency diagnostics for modifier screening, but it does not by itself provide or validate a maintained implementation.
queue.design_sketch: Simulate connected networks while varying the magnitude and sign of direct-versus-indirect treatment-covariate interaction inconsistency, covariate variation, and trial count; compare node-splitting and design-by-treatment diagnostics on type I error, power, and downstream bias and coverage of target-population effects.
queue.priority_note: Run early because inconsistent modifier evidence can invalidate ML-NMR adjustment and the question has measurable operating characteristics.

queue.title: Baseline risk is not a neutral anchor for disconnected evidence
queue.answerable_part: Simulation can compare baseline-bridge estimators under explicit prognostic, design, and measurement-error mechanisms, but disconnected data cannot validate the cross-gap exchangeability assumption itself.
queue.design_sketch: Vary cross-study prognostic imbalance, endpoint or follow-up shifts, baseline-risk measurement error, and commensurability while estimating a target-population marginal treatment effect. Compare fully exchangeable, separate, covariate-conditioned, and commensurate baseline models on bias, coverage, decision error, and posterior dependence on the baseline bridge.
queue.priority_note: This is a useful focused simulation, but existing evidence already shows severe misspecification risk, so it ranks below genuinely unevaluated PAIC questions.

queue.title: Single shared heterogeneity variance across classes and populations
queue.answerable_part: A simulation can give useful design-specific thresholds for distinguishing variance structures, but no universal minimum network size exists independently of heterogeneity magnitude, prior information and allocation of studies across classes.
queue.design_sketch: Estimate target-population treatment effects under common, class-specific and exchangeable heterogeneity structures while varying studies per class, true variance ratios and prior informativeness. Use selection accuracy, heterogeneity-parameter coverage and treatment-effect coverage to identify when the structures become practically distinguishable.
queue.priority_note: Although rated high, this is less urgent than identification diagnostics because its answer will be scenario-dependent, but it remains a clean simulation if restricted to realistic ML-NMR network sizes.

queue.title: Outcome ascertainment and the observation process in external data
queue.answerable_part: A simulation can quantify and correct selected combinations of assessment timing, event misclassification and informative visiting, but cannot identify their sensitivity parameters from aggregate comparator data.
queue.design_sketch: Estimate a target-population restricted mean survival-time difference while varying assessment interval, event sensitivity and specificity, recording lag and dependence of visit intensity on latent disease progression. Compare naive, interval-censored and joint observation-process analyses on bias, coverage and sensitivity to misspecified observation models.
queue.priority_note: The problem is important but should follow simpler survival QBA studies because the interacting latent event and observation processes make it a poor early experiment.

queue.title: Constancy assumptions are never tested across calendar time
queue.answerable_part: Repeated temporal holdouts can estimate context-specific out-of-time prediction error and drift, but they cannot isolate a universal coefficient-decay rate or justify a general trial-age cutoff.
queue.design_sketch: Fit population-adjusted outcome and effect-modifier models to trials available before each calendar cutoff, standardize predictions to the later trial population, and compare predicted marginal arm outcomes and relative effects with the later randomized results. Relate uncertainty-aware prediction error to calendar gap after modeling sampling error, ordinary heterogeneity, overlap, and recorded design changes.
queue.priority_note: The question is valuable but should not run early because repeated estimand-aligned IPD holdouts and separation of temporal drift from heterogeneity require substantial data and modeling work.

queue.title: Change scores, trajectories, and responder-threshold estimands
queue.answerable_part: A focused study can answer when endpoint and change-score population adjustment diverge under baseline effect modification; trajectories and latent-model responder probabilities require separate designs and richer data.
queue.design_sketch: Vary baseline-target distribution shift, baseline prognostic strength, baseline-by-treatment interaction and baseline-follow-up correlation, then compare change-score and endpoint PAIC estimators on bias and coverage for the target follow-up mean contrast.
queue.priority_note: The broad entry is overstated, but its change-versus-endpoint adjustment component is a clean, feasible experiment that could run early.

queue.title: Risk-modeling network meta-regression treats a fitted risk score as observed
queue.answerable_part: A study can quantify interval undercoverage from treating the fitted risk score as observed and show the practical effect of propagating uncertainty, but it cannot settle the transportability assumptions needed to identify a fully joint model.
queue.design_sketch: Vary prognostic-model sample size, calibration drift, score shrinkage, and target risk percentile; compare plug-in, bootstrap, and joint ML-NMR estimates on bias and coverage of risk-specific treatment effects, then reanalyze a published dataset to measure interval widening at median and tail risks.
queue.priority_note: This is a relevant and feasible early study if restricted to uncertainty propagation; the broader joint-model identification problem should be deferred.

queue.title: Unequal variances, skew, and bounded scales in continuous outcomes
queue.answerable_part: A simulation can quantify the consequences of common-variance and normality assumptions for selected marginal, predictive or responder estimands; it cannot identify skewness or boundary masses in aggregate trials that report only means and standard deviations.
queue.design_sketch: Vary study-specific variance ratios, skewness, floor or ceiling mass and source-target overlap, then compare common-normal, hierarchical-variance and support-respecting likelihoods on bias and coverage for the target mean and responder probability. The contrast between stable mean estimates and distorted responder estimates would test the claimed estimand dependence.
queue.priority_note: This is worthwhile after selecting one bounded endpoint and one non-mean estimand; the full entry is too heterogeneous for an early single study.

queue.title: Evidence-provenance measures do not propagate heterogeneity uncertainty
queue.answerable_part: A study can quantify how variance-component uncertainty changes PAIC contribution or borrowing measures, but it cannot supply valid uncertainty intervals before the underlying Bayesian contribution functional is defined.
queue.design_sketch: Simulate sparse ML-NMR networks while varying true heterogeneity, study count, and heterogeneity-prior informativeness, then measure changes in source contributions across posterior draws of variance components. Reanalyze several published networks and record changes in the leading contributor and borrowing shares.
queue.priority_note: Do not run first for PAIC because the contribution quantity itself needs definition before uncertainty around it is interpretable.
